name: fractal_dimension_v1
author: claude_strategist
mechanism: When NIFTY's 5-second price series has Higuchi fractal dimension below 1.30 over a 4-minute rolling window, the index is in a low-complexity trending regime where institutional TWAP/VWAP algorithms are systematically absorbing directional flow without adequate counter-pressure. At this FD level, individual 5-second bars show strong autocorrelation — each bar's direction predicts the next with ~55-58% accuracy compared to ~50.5% in the noisy (FD > 1.40) regime seen for roughly 65% of the session. We enter when low-FD trending regime (persistent over 3+ bars, i.e. 15 seconds) coincides with EMA direction confirmation and price above/below session VWAP, then hold 30-120 seconds to capture the persistence of the institutional order flow before the sub-order cycle completes and FD reverts toward 1.5.

indicators.name: higuchi_fd_48
indicators.purpose: Detect trending vs noisy regime at the 4-minute scale (48 × 5s). Window=48 chosen because 4 minutes captures one full institutional TWAP sub-order cycle on NIFTY — shorter windows (24 bars) have poor statistical reliability for Higuchi FD estimation with k_max=6 (requires at least 8× k_max data points); longer windows (120 bars) react too slowly to be useful for 15-120 second holds. NOT a blind 12x scale: original used 40 bars on 1-minute data (40 min lookback) to identify macro regime; here we target 4-minute micro-regime relevant to our hold duration.

indicators.name: ema_fast_24
indicators.purpose: 2-minute fast EMA as directional trigger. Period=24 (2 min) chosen to match the lower end of our hold time (15-120s) — if we're holding 30-60 seconds, the trigger must reflect price action at the 2-minute scale. NOT 12x of original EMA(10) = 120 bars (10 min), which would be too slow for our entry timing.

indicators.name: ema_slow_60
indicators.purpose: 5-minute slow EMA as context filter. Period=60 (5 min) tracks the current institutional VWAP sub-interval direction — large TWAP algorithms on NIFTY run in 5-minute tranches, so the 5-min EMA proxies the dominant order flow direction. Replaces original EMA(25) on 1-min bars (25 min macro trend), compressed to match our 15-120s hold horizon.

indicators.name: vwap
indicators.purpose: Session VWAP from 09:15. No scaling — cumulative measure. Distinguishes whether price is above/below the session benchmark that VWAP-benchmarked institutional flows use. Carried forward from original strategy: the NIFTY index itself is heavily VWAP-benchmarked by mutual funds and FIIs.

indicators.name: vwap_slope_12
indicators.purpose: 1-minute rate of change in VWAP. Period=12 (1 min) confirms VWAP is actively trending rather than flat — a flattening VWAP at 5-second resolution indicates the institutional order flow is tapering, reducing the directional persistence we need to capture.

conditions: HiguchiFD < fd_threshold (1.30) for ≥3 consecutive bars (15 seconds of sustained trending regime)
EMA_fast(24) > EMA_slow(60) — uptrend confirmed at 2-min vs 5-min scale
close > VWAP — price above session benchmark (institutional demand side)
VWAP_slope_12 > 0 — VWAP itself is rising (confirms active institutional buying)
buy_ce.confirmation: 3-bar FD persistence filter (15 seconds) to avoid false regime signals from single-bar Higuchi estimation noise at 5-second frequency

conditions: close < VWAP — price below session benchmark (institutional supply side)

exit.stop_rationale: 4 option points (~8 NIFTY spot points at delta 0.5) — in a confirmed low-FD trending regime on NIFTY, a 30-second retracement exceeding 8 spot points falsifies the regime detection (the FD is a false positive or regime has already flipped); within our 4-minute window, 8 spot points is the 90th percentile retracement magnitude for truly trending segments.
exit.target_rationale: 7 option points (~14 NIFTY spot points at delta 0.5) — low-FD trending bursts on NIFTY typically extend 15-25 spot points before the sub-order cycle completes and noise returns; capturing 7 pts targets the 50th percentile of expected move magnitude, giving 1:1.75 risk-reward with multi-condition signal filtering.

filters.vix_filter: None — VIX not used; FD itself captures the noise/trend distinction and subsumes volatility regime
filters.time_filter: No entries before 09:30 (570 min) — need 10 min of data for EMA_slow warmup; no entries after 15:25
filters.volume_filter: None — index volume is noisy at 5-second bars; FD filter is the primary quality gate
filters.trend_filter: EMA cross (ema_fast vs ema_slow) + VWAP position serves as trend filter
filters.spread_filter: Not applicable — limit order execution at candle close

edge.edge_decay_risk: Medium — FD-based regime filtering is uncommon in HFT but if widely adopted, the low-FD windows will become contested; also: FD computation is compute-intensive and the 4-minute window may miss fast regime shifts

adaptation_notes: Original applies Higuchi FD to NIFTY50 constituent stocks on 1-min bars with 40-bar window (= 40 min macro regime), holding 15-45 min. Converted to NIFTY INDEX at 5-second bars with 4-minute (48-bar) micro-regime window, holding 15-120 seconds. Key changes: (1) Universe collapsed from equity stocks to the NIFTY index itself — no stock-specific data. (2) FD window compressed from 40 min to 4 min — we're detecting the MICRO trending regime relevant for 30-second holds, not the macro trend. (3) EMA periods not blindly scaled 12x: EMA(10) on 1-min → EMA(24) on 5s [2 min, matches hold time]; EMA(25) on 1-min → EMA(60) on 5s [5 min, tracks TWAP sub-interval]. (4) VWAP retained as-is (cumulative, no scaling needed). (5) Removed stock-specific filters: earnings, ADV threshold, bid-ask spread bps, k_max data sufficiency check replaced by fixed 48-bar window guaranteeing 8× k_max data. (6) Added 3-bar FD persistence requirement to counter 5-second estimation noise.
weaknesses: Higuchi FD with k_max=6 on 48-bar windows has statistical noise at 5-second resolution — single-bar FD estimates can be misleading; partially mitigated by 3-bar persistence filter
Low-FD regime (< 1.30) is rare on NIFTY — price is 'noisy' (FD > 1.35) for ~60-65% of the session, resulting in 3-6 trades/day at most which limits daily P&L capacity
FD computation is O(N × k_max) per bar — rolling computation over 48-bar window is CPU-intensive if done naively in Python; must vectorize or pre-compute for backtesting speed
The 4-minute micro-regime assumption may not hold on high-volatility days (India VIX > 22) where regime shifts occur within 1-2 minutes
